newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury not too worried by Social Chapter.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury not too worried by Social Chapter.

text.p: A director of J. Sainsbury Plc told Conservative members of parliament on Tuesday he was not greatly concerned at this stage about two of their bugbears -- a minimum wage and the European Union's Social Chapter.

John Adshead, in charge of the supermarket group's personnel and training, was pressed on the two issues by Conservatives Harry Greenway and Sir Ralph Howell when he appeared before parliament's Education and Employment sub-committee.
The Conservatives claim that Labour's plans to introduce a national minimum wage and end Britain's Social Chapter opt-out will push up labour costs and force up unemployment.
But Adshead told Greenway the Social Chapter only contained two relatively minor regulations as yet, on parental leave and on works councils for transnational companies.
"So far on the legislation I have been presented with -- in my view it will not have a very serious impact on our business," he said.
But he added: "That is not to say that in the future the European Union and the European Commission will not come up with something that is harmful to our business. They may well do."
Questioned by both Howell and Greenway on the minimum wage, Adshead said he did not have enough information on how it would work to judge its likely impact.
"The devil is in the detail. Until we get some detail it is very difficult to respond," he said.

"It is about how it is organised, what it includes, what it is based on, how it is enforced, whether there are regional differences, how it affects young people and so on...these are things that all need to be determined," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
